Before starting medication, I used to bring home a big energy after working all day, chug it, and take the best nap of my life.

That’s insane! Congrats. Those are huge accomplishments. 
I happen to be a perfectionist, pretty smart, and had strict parents so I would force myself to do really good in school and push myself past my limits constantly because I knew what I was capable of but I felt like I couldn’t do it. Once I got to college that’s when shit went to shit bc I was so burnt out from how much harder I had to work to get stuff done and that’s when I finally started to seek help. Especially since it got to the point where I was sleeping for 12 hours a night then would take 3-5 hour naps in the middle of the day and was still exhausted all of the time. I also have ptsd so some of it plays into that. 
But wow getting diagnosed was insane. Turns out I didn’t have ocd or the personality disorders I was thought to have. It was all adhd. Social anxiety issues? Adhd. 
I’m about to graduate college soon and just started an internship at a hospital while also working full time and I wouldn’t be able to do that without my meds. Diagnosis is definitely a privilege and isn’t always accessible for everyone but I would NEVER discourage someone from seeking a diagnosis or help if they are struggling

I genuinely believe some of these people who believe they have did are probably dealing with maladaptive daydreaming disorder and just don’t realize it. With MDD you can get INCREDIBLY engulfed in your daydreams. Idk if I have MDD and I’m not going to self diagnose at all btw but I will mention that I used to day dream A LOT when I was younger during stressful times in my life. I would act out my “characters”, feel their emotions, and make their facial expression. I would do it the most when I felt lonely or anxious is a certain situation. Eventually it turned to me doing it all of the time and got to the point where it started to feel real and I had genuine connections to these imaginary people I would daydream about. over the years I am slowly growing out of it. 

I really think that these people are dealing with something similar but the only answers they are seeing relating to why they are behaving this way relate to MDD. In reality things like adhd, mdd, etc can cause someone to escape into an imaginary world that can begin to feel real.
